parole.significato: A nocturnal dance held by Aboriginal Australians, for social, celebratory or warlike purposes.

parole.significato: A group of Aboriginal people traditionally inhabiting what is now Sydney, New South Wales, Australia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Dharug gadigal, from gadi (“below, under”) + -gal (gentilic suffix), literally “the people below”, referring to the people who belonged to the land below Port Jackson.

parole.significato: A plant of the genus Persoonia.

An Aboriginal woman.

parole.significato: A traditional Aboriginal dwelling made of bark and sticks.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Dharug gunya (“shelter”), first recorded 1803.

parole.significato: A footprint.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Dharug mari, maray (“great, very”). First attested in 1818.

A wild dingo.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Dharug wuragal (“wild and undomesticated dingo”).
